nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: 28 kWh pack of the same car (pack voltage not on its ArenaEV page): the 38.3 kWh pack is 320 V (ArenaEV) and Hyundai-Kia 800 V only arrived with E-GMP (2021).

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: no page for the Ioniq Electric describes a battery warming or conditioning feature (Hyundai UK press kit and US 2020 release do not mention one), and Hyundai Motor Group presents navigation-triggered battery conditioning as new with the 2022-2023 IONIQ 5, years after this car. Caveat: Canadian Ioniq Electrics may have had a battery heater (the Kona Electric did); not checked.

capacity_gross_kwh.notes: ArenaEV: 30.5 kWh total (Fastned also lists 30.5 kWh for 2016-2019).

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: ArenaEV: 28 kWh usable (Hyundai states a 28 kWh battery).

chemistry.notes: ADAC manufacturer-data table for the 28 kWh Ioniq Elektro (11/16-07/19): Nickel-Mangan-Cobalt; EVSpecifications 2019 (LG Chem, NCM LiNiCoMnO2) agrees. The 2017-2019 North American cars use the same 28 kWh pack (nothing found to show a change).

ac_max_kw.notes: US 2017 car: 6.6 kW J1772 onboard charger (Wikipedia: 6.6 kW 2016-2019). Canadian figure assumed the same.

dc_max_kw.notes: Fastned: max charge speed 70 kW for the 30.5 kWh car (ArenaEV also 70 kW). Hyundai says the inlet accepts 100 kW chargers (80 % in about 23 min on a 100 kW charger), which is the charger rating, not the car.
